title: Maximize Tax Savings: Understanding Section 80C Deductions

faq.q: What is the maximum deduction allowed under Section 80C?
faq.a: The maximum deduction allowed under Section 80C for a financial year is ₹1.5 lakh. This limit applies to the combined total of all eligible investments and expenses.

faq.q: Who is eligible to claim Section 80C deduction?
faq.a: Individuals and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) are eligible to claim deductions under Section 80C. Companies and firms are not eligible.

faq.q: Can I claim Section 80C benefits under both old and new tax regimes?
faq.a: No, the deductions under Section 80C are only available if you opt for the old tax regime. The new tax regime, introduced from FY 2020-21, does not allow most deductions, including those under Section 80C.

faq.q: Is interest earned on PPF taxable?
faq.a: No, the interest earned on Public Provident Fund (PPF) is entirely tax-exempt. PPF falls under the EEE (Exempt-Exempt-Exempt) category, meaning contributions, interest, and maturity amounts are all tax-free.

faq.q: What is the lock-in period for ELSS funds?
faq.a: Equity-Linked Savings Schemes (ELSS) have a mandatory lock-in period of three years from the date of investment. This is the shortest lock-in period among all Section 80C investment options.

faq.q: Are all fixed deposits eligible for Section 80C?
faq.a: No, only specific tax-saving fixed deposits with a lock-in period of five years, offered by banks and post offices, are eligible for deduction under Section 80C. Regular fixed deposits do not qualify.

faq.q: Can I claim tuition fees for my spouse's education under Section 80C?
faq.a: No, Section 80C only allows deduction for tuition fees paid for the full-time education of up to two children. Fees paid for your own or your spouse's education are not eligible.
